newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks close at record highs.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks close at record highs.

text.p: Swiss shares ended Friday at a record highs for the second day in a row in active trade.
Share dealers said the dollar's strength, as well as short covering tied options and futures expiry on the Swiss futures exchange Soffex, drove the market higher.
The broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) ended 23.05 points higher at a new closing high at 2,486.68
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) was also up 41.5 points at 3,897.9, setting a new closing high after it hit an all-time high of 3,902.1 during the session.
SMI December futures were also up 42 at 3,908.
Sentiment remained bullish, with some traders believing the SMI could reach 4,000 points soon.

Activity was lively in CS Holding, which rose 3.75 Swiss francs to 136.25. Markets were waiting for the group to release its nine-month figures, which are expected on Monday. Markets are also waiting for news on progress of restructuring at the banking concern.
CS Holding declines to comment on market rumours. Its gains also boosted other banking stocks.
Union Bank of Switzerland added six to 1,257, while Swiss Bank Corp gained 3.75 to 253.25.
Dealers said dollar-earners were driven higher by the the U.S. currency's latest strength versus the Swiss franc.
Nestle added 12 francs to 1,433. Roche firmed 80 to 9,925. Dealers said Nestle and Roche were also driven higher by Soffex-related short covering.

Dealers said many investors may also perceive the Swiss market, apart from a few highflyers like Novartis or Roche, as having thus far had only moderate gains. This could argue for more gains before year-end, they said.
Cyclical shares, especially those with business in Germany, were in demand as the Swiss franc continued to weaken against the German mark. Alusuisse rose eight to 990.
Among insurers, Swiss Re was 18 francs higher at 1,413, just below an all-time high of 1,415 set earlier in the day.
Zurich Insurance, up five to 369, also saw a new year high.
Trading on Soffex was moderately active. Dealers said futures and options expiry went smoothly.
Late trade grew livelier after U.S. economic data, which prompted gains as some short covering emerged, dealers said.

The expiring November SMI futures contract was settled at 3,885.4. Trade in CS Holding, SBG, Nestle and Winterthur options was active. SMI options traded volume was 55,160 contracts. Volatility was slightly lower.
